routing_warnings.description: The instruction to emphasize the hero's first sentence rather than its tagline concerns the independently defined hero presentation.
The decision to carry the dark theme across later website pages primarily establishes the shared website page theme rather than changing the landing-page visual direction.
The reported removal of top navigation belongs to the website header-navigation Requirement.
The reported removal of footer links belongs to the shared website-footer Requirement.
The prevention of hero-text and image overlap concerns the hero presentation.
The added mid-resolution breakpoint and improved laptop display concern responsive layout behavior.
The client's acceptance of the general responsive breakpoint guidance applies to the reusable guidance Requirement rather than specifically modifying the landing-page responsive implementation.
The same message separately reports removing footer links.
The same message separately establishes a plan to add navigation links to the footer.
The same message also reports removal of the top navigation, which belongs to the website header-navigation Requirement.
The client's agreement to omit header navigation should also be evaluated under the website header-navigation Requirement.

The active-node accent choice, wizard-specific layout variables, Back/Next interaction states, and temporary chevron concern apply specifically to provisioning-wizard styling rather than the reusable design-token specification.
The remaining shade and tone polishing concerns the Admin Workspace rather than the website design-token specification.
The message says responsiveness was considered in the landing-page layout and does not establish reusable breakpoint guidance.
The delivered desktop, tablet, and mobile styling is specific to the landing page rather than general breakpoint guidance.
The mid-resolution breakpoint addresses hero overlap on the landing page and is narrower than reusable website-wide guidance.
The approval and alternative-background offer concern the specialized sign-in page rather than the reusable informational-page shell.
This message asks whether implementation code is required for the sign-in and provisioning pages; it concerns the separate prototype-code deliverable.
The proposal to create separate coded pages concerns the task-local prototype-code deliverable.
The client authorizes optional rough code for the additional pages, establishing the separate prototype-code deliverable.
The clause about customizing the Cognito-generated sign-in page and its intended background belongs to the specialized sign-in branding Requirement.
The clause stating that the same background is used for the Tenant Launch Flow concerns provisioning-wizard styling.
The temporary PDF-in-new-tab behavior for Cookie and Privacy pages belongs to the policy-document access Requirement.
The completed sign-in-page design claim belongs to the specialized Cognito sign-in branding Requirement.
Delivery of the Sign In page background image belongs to the specialized Cognito sign-in branding Requirement.

The background, header-logo, and possible-footer treatment concerns the shared minimal shell around informational and provisioning pages rather than the wizard-specific progress, panel, and control styling.
The optional request to rough out code for additional pages is a task-local prototype-code deliverable rather than a change to the persistent wizard styling.
The completed design presented here is explicitly for the sign-in page, not the provisioning wizard.
The discussion concerns placement and interaction of shell and application navigation panels rather than the shell's general visual styling.
The proposed nested single-panel structure belongs to the independent panel-navigation Requirement.
Avoiding competing panels and evaluating a nested menu concerns panel-navigation architecture.
The button color, shape, size, rounding, and icon questions belong to the independent button-styling Requirement; only the Admin Workspace naming change applies to the target.
The freelancer's recommendations concern the independent Admin Workspace button treatment.
The observation that other console interfaces use monochrome buttons is evidence for the button-styling Requirement, not a shell-wide styling change.
The submitted Admin Workspace UI design is described broadly and does not specifically identify the button treatment.
The client's settled look-and-feel statement concerns the Admin Workspace generally and does not explicitly resolve the button-specific decisions.
The clause requiring clockwise directional arrows applies to the second, cyclic-process diagram rather than the target interaction diagram.
The customer and staff channel labels in this message apply to the first, omnichannel interaction diagram rather than the target cyclic-process diagram.
